Description of contribution in a few bullet points


This PR solves the problem with costmap_2d_publisher, which appeared from Jazzy. The problem is that the costmap is never published on its topic, if there aren't any subscribers on the topic before launching Nav2 nodes. The problem is described more in its related issue (#6267).

To solve this problem, I moved the grid parameter update inside the if statement which examines whether there are any subscribers on the costmap topic. This is the exact behavior as in Iron and older distributions.

There is no need to update the documentation.

This change was tested on my own real robot. I followed the exact same steps I described in the issue (#6267) under reproduction steps and instructions.

@SteveMacenski I signed off on DCO, but other than that, I didn't have time to examine the failure in greater detail. As I looked at it now, it is strange to me. I think my change should not cause any build problems.

The current build failure is not your own, its due to some rolling API changes I'm working on right now. But the last time this ran in CI, a bunch of functional system tests failed (compilation worked) due to your changes. You should be able to see that locally running colcon test --packages-select nav2_costmap_2d nav2_system_tests. It may take ~15-20 minutes since the system tests run several full simulations.


I'm pretty confident from that CI run that there's a functional problem in your solution

An issue, predating these changes, that jumps to my eyes is that the grid varaibles

grid_width_, grid_height_ ...

are uninitialized variables during the first comparison -> There is a possible undefined behavior. Moving the initialization within the if, lets them stay uninitialized for longer, but my gut feeling is that it shouldn't have a largely negative impact.


I would



Init those variables (ex directly in the header to 0 values)

Optional:


To make the initialization a bit more explicit/readable, add a boolean variable (costmap_published_once_{false};) to explicitally forbid the update path until it is published once.



@TZalan0814 do you want to give it a try or should I go for it?
